title: dYdX chain — ibc-go v8.5.1 halt advisory (ISA-2025-001/ASA-2025-004) is neutralized by the vendored dydxprotocol/ibc-go fork; no theft primitive, capture negative EV
closed_reasons: Live dYdX v9.7.0/9.7.1 binaries build github.com/cosmos/ibc-go/v8 v8.5.1 as a REPLACED module (empty sum in build info, 4 independent endpoints) pointing to github.com/dydxprotocol/ibc-go/v8 v8.0.0-rc.0.0.20250312180215-8733b3edf43a (git commit 8733b3edf43a5fa412e65e0cc2ad75c3902b9014, 2025-03-12T18:02:15Z)

That exact commit contains BOTH advisory fixes: ASA-2025-004 transfer check (modules/apps/transfer/ibc_module.go line 247: 'acknowledgement did not marshal to expected bytes') and ISA-2025-001 core check (modules/core/04-channel/keeper/packet.go line 435: 'acknowledgement marshalling error', inside AcknowledgePacket @ line 358)

The content-addressed module zip from proxy.golang.org for that pseudo-version contains both fix markers and its dirhash h1:aF1rORtUApr+N6dWsNiT/G9H2ysfjyj5DiVRU8CRDaU= matches the go.sum entry in dydxprotocol/v4-chain protocol/v9.7.1 — the exact artifact the live binary was built against is patched

Release matrix: dYdX pinned upstream ibc-go v8.0.0 (vulnerable to both) through protocol/v8.0.6; fork e238a5667825 (ASA fixed, ISA not) at v8.0.7 (2025-02-28); fork 8733b3edf43a (both fixed) at every release from v8.0.8 (2025-03-12) through v9.7.1
No ack-deserializing IBC middleware on dYdX (no ibc-hooks, no packet-forward-middleware, no wasm in the 247 build deps) — the advisory's middleware caveat does not apply
Halt class has no theft/fund-loss primitive; a rejected ack is a normal failed tx and the chain keeps producing blocks

poc.note: Cosmos chain — no EVM fork; verification is source/marker + live build-info re-derivation in ci/verify.py (CI success; both fork fix markers present = true at height 108,686,391)

key_facts: Corpus flag 'ibc-go v8.5.1' matches the vulnerable ranges by version STRING only: ASA-2025-004 affects ibc-go <8.6.1 (v8 line) and ISA-2025-001 affects v8 >=8.0.0-alpha.1 <8.7.0; the effective code is the patched fork, not upstream v8.5.1

Advisory text: 'Any user that can open an IBC channel can introduce this state' — on dYdX channel opening is permissionless (MsgChannelOpenInit is a normal user msg; only IBC params-updates are gov-only internal msgs), so the precondition exists, but the vulnerable code path is closed by the fork

Fix semantics: reject acknowledgements whose canonical re-marshalling differs from supplied bytes (round-trip byte equality) — v8.6.1 transfer module (ASA-2025-004), v8.7.0 core AcknowledgePacket for all apps (ISA-2025-001)

Live IBC state (2026-10-09): 123 channels (76 OPEN, 42 CLOSED, 5 TRYOPEN; icahost 83, transfer 40), 47 connections (40 OPEN); Noble USDC via transfer/channel-0 with 70,772,323.76 USDC total supply on chain; stDYDX via channel-1

Gov quorum was raised to 0.5 by prop 392 (passed 2026-08-03, 'Increase Governance Quorum to 50%'): quorum votes = 0.5 x 285,934,158.72 bonded DYDX = 142,967,079 DYDX ~ $19.42M at $0.13582 (3.29x 24h volume) vs ~$23.33M nominal gov-spendable (community treasury 79,763,439 DYDX ~ $10.83M; rewards treasury 32,485,307 DYDX ~ $4.41M; insurance fund 8,080,668.51 USDC ~ $8.08M; community pool ~$0.0002M) — negative EV after slippage, 21-day unbonding and 33.4% veto; spendability code-verified via gov-only dydxprotocol.sending.MsgSendFromModuleToAccount (prop 390 precedent spent from community_treasury)

Bridge module account (41,657,038 DYDX ~ $5.66M user-backed escrow) is not in the protected-modules list ({bonded_tokens_pool, not_bonded_tokens_pool, subaccounts}) — flagged as a broader governance-authority observation, not counted in the capture headline
Halt-damage context (not profit): 70,772,323.76 USDC on-chain + ~$38.95M total perp open interest (dYdX indexer, 296 markets) would freeze during a halt; attacker gain $0

Software-upgrade history: prop 395 -> v9.7 (height 105,002,000, live now); prop 398 'Software Upgrade v9.8' in voting at read time (submitted 2026-10-08, ends 2026-10-11T02:23Z, plan height 109,170,000, yes 161.4M / abstain 15.5M / no 0, quorum met; binaries v9.8.0-9ab4e17a; source not yet public); current_plan = null

Live node reads (2026-10-09): app 9.7.1 @ publicnode (git 5935cb7c5dd684b17836e75093fc5c3ca5019ea3) and 9.7.0 @ polkachu (git 67a3c71670c460ef92ffb15930dda7047a901f64); ibc-go/v8 v8.5.1 sum empty (replaced; cosmos-sdk/cometbft/iavl likewise replaced)

Fork security timeline: ASA-2025-004 fix cherry-picked 2025-02-28 (e238a5667825 'fix: remove packet data remarshaling (#8065)'); ISA-2025-001 fix merged 2025-03-12 (8b909d54ce09, tip 8733b3edf43a PGP-signed) — both same-day as advisory publication
caveats: Build deps are self-reported by nodes; corroborated on 4 independent endpoints + pinned go.mod + go.sum dirhash match against the proxy module zip — no reproducible binary build was performed
The exact internal Go-JSON divergence mechanism is not spelled out publicly; the fix (round-trip byte equality) is the authoritative statement of the vulnerable condition
USD values are point-in-time (2026-10-09 ~07:00Z; DYDX $0.13582 from DefiLlama/CoinGecko; CoinGecko mcap field was inconsistent with the 1e27 adydx supply and was ignored)

The fork base is upstream ibc-go v8.0.0 + dYdX cherry-picks: upstream v8 security fixes are not automatically present unless cherry-picked (both published v8 halt advisories are); v9.8.0 source/binary pin should be re-checked once public
Insurance-fund/rewards-treasury/bridge spendability is code-path verified but has no governance precedent; 'capturable in principle' is not 'politically passable'

gov_capture.verdict: negative EV (cost >= $19.42M at spot and realistically more due to 3.29x ADV impact; 21-day unbonding; 33.4% veto; 87% of pot is DYDX whose liquidation would crater price)
gov_capture.confidence: high on parameters; medium on slippage/realizable value

one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract $0 live from the dYdX chain ibc-go halt advisory: the live v9.7.x binary is built from the dydxprotocol/ibc-go fork commit 8733b3edf43a (go.sum-pinned, both ASA-2025-004 and ISA-2025-001 fix checks present, in place since protocol v8.0.8 on 2025-03-12), so the permissionlessly-reachable crafted-ack halt vector is closed; DoS monetization is $0 (no theft primitive) and gov capture (~$19.4M quorum cost at spot / 3.29x ADV vs ~$23.3M nominal pots) is negative EV.
